description: Eight sourced photographs and micrographs for Earth life and simple physical structures. Every source page documents the author and CC0 or CC BY-SA conditions. Scientific interpretation remains under editorial review.

images.title: Bees on a hexagonal wax honeycomb
images.summary: Honeybees cluster on a wax comb inside a beekeeper's Langstroth frame. The repeating cells offer an accessible example of hexagonal organization in the natural world.
images.alt: A vertical wooden beehive frame full of hexagonal wax cells, with many honeybees crawling across the comb.
images.caption: Honeybees and their wax construction; a managed hive and human-made wooden frame are visible, but the hexagonal comb itself was built by insects.
images.rights: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0); link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ . Photo © Benlisquare; this re-encoded derivative is likewise CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution and modification notice required.
images.processing: The original photograph was sourced from Wikimedia Commons and resized to a maximum side length of 1800 pixels; its colors were retained and a JPEG quality-87 derivative was made for the development ZIP. The source page links to the uploaded original.

images.title: A snow crystal under magnification
images.summary: Wilson Alwyn Bentley documented the intricate sixfold form of one natural snow crystal through photomicrography. The original historic image is preserved by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
images.alt: An intricate six-armed white snow crystal with branching internal patterns, centered in a black circle on cream photographic paper.
images.caption: Snow crystals reflect the molecular organization of frozen water and environmental growth conditions. One real crystal is shown rather than an idealized diagram.
images.credit: Wilson Alwyn Bentley / The Metropolitan Museum of Art
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; see individual Wikimedia Commons file page for license declaration. Attribution retained as archival provenance.

images.title: Cultured bacteria viewed through an optical microscope
images.summary: An amateur microscopy photograph, taken at a stated 100×, shows numerous violet-stained bacteria from a sample cultured from fermented pickles. Gram-stain interpretation is reported by the photographer and awaits specialist verification.
images.alt: Dense small violet rodlike forms scattered across a bright circular microscope field.
images.caption: This microscope image demonstrates cellular organisms too small to observe individually unaided. The specimen identification, staining and magnification are reported by the uploader, not independently validated.

images.title: Mushrooms on a forest floor
images.summary: Several unidentified mushrooms are photographed among trees and leaf litter in a forest. Their fruiting bodies represent one visible stage in a fungal life cycle.
images.alt: Brown mushrooms with broad overlapping caps growing from the leaf-covered forest floor beneath trees.
images.caption: Mushrooms are reproductive fruiting bodies of fungi. Although many fungi decompose organic material, the exact identity and ecological role of these mushrooms is unverified.

images.title: Fern fronds in sunlight
images.summary: Feathery green fern leaves photographed in San Francisco exemplify the complex fronds of spore-bearing vascular plants. Mosses, a different major lineage, are not shown in this particular frame.
images.alt: Detailed green fern fronds with delicate branching leaflets brightly lit by sunlight, in front of dark brown wooden boards.
images.caption: A fern specimen illustrates a lineage of vascular plants that reproduces by spores. The broader image slot also calls for mosses, which remain to be documented separately.
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; see individual Wikimedia Commons file page for license declaration. Attribution retained as archival provenance.

The source page links to the uploaded original. A Wikimedia 1280-pixel derivative was the source for local JPEG processing.

images.title: A butterfly visits flowering plants
images.summary: A large yellow-and-black butterfly rests on a group of flowers, illustrating the ecological relationship between insects and flowering plants. Whether pollen transfer occurred in this instant cannot be established from the photograph alone.
images.alt: Yellow and black butterfly perched on red flowers in front of many white blossoms.
images.caption: An insect feeding or resting on a flowering plant can visit multiple flowers and, for some species, transfer pollen. This photograph does not prove a particular pollination event.

images.title: Fish beneath the water surface
images.summary: Several fish are photographed in shallow river water, illustrating the aquatic context in which these animals move and feed. The particular location and fish species are not identified.
images.alt: Several pale fish swimming above a light sandy riverbed in clear blue-tinted water.
images.caption: Photographed fish underwater in a river. The uploader did not establish a precise species identification or river location.

images.title: Frog in a freshwater pond
images.summary: A frog partly submerged amid aquatic vegetation illustrates amphibian adaptations to wetland environments.
images.alt: Green and mottled frog with eyes above shallow pond water, surrounded by long green aquatic plants.
images.caption: Amphibians occupy environments that connect land and water; many species depend on aquatic habitats during their life cycles. The species pictured here was not independently identified.
